This page compares the scenarios in [scenarios.yml](../scenarios.yml), using
the outputs in [results/](../results). Run `make` from the repository root to
render every scenario and this page. Each scenario has its own report:

```{r}
library(data.table)
scenarios <- yaml::read_yaml("../scenarios.yml")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  scenario    = sprintf("[%s](%s.md)", names(scenarios), names(scenarios)),
  response    = vapply(scenarios, `[[`, "", "response"),
  description = vapply(scenarios, `[[`, "", "description")
), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
replicates <- rbindlist(lapply(names(scenarios), function(s) {
  fread(file.path("../results", s, "replicates.csv"))
}))
metadata <- rbindlist(lapply(names(scenarios), function(s) {
  fread(file.path("../results", s, "metadata.csv"))[, scenario := s]
}))
metadata <- dcast(metadata, scenario ~ name, value.var = "value")

# Pairing needs the same replicates and calibration in every scenario.
stopifnot(
  length(unique(metadata$replicates)) == 1,
  length(unique(metadata$transmission_rate)) == 1
)
```

All scenarios share `r metadata$replicates[1]` replicates, the same
population, vaccination and calibrated transmission rate
(`r signif(as.numeric(metadata$transmission_rate[1]), 3)` per contact).
Counts are for the `r format(as.numeric(metadata$n[1]), big.mark = ",")`-agent
model; multiply by `r round(as.numeric(metadata$county_scale[1]), 2)` for
Salt Lake County.

## Outcomes by scenario

Means per replicate, with medians of infections; most introductions stay
small, so means are driven by the outbreaks that grow.

```{r}
replicates[, scenario := factor(scenario, levels = names(scenarios))]
knitr::kable(
  replicates[, .(
    infections_mean       = mean(infections),
    infections_median     = as.numeric(median(infections)),
    infections_q90        = quantile(infections, 0.9),
    admissions            = mean(admissions),
    hospital_days         = mean(hospital_days),
    excluded_student_days = mean(excluded_student_days),
    samples               = mean(samples),
    alert_days            = mean(alert_days),
    false_positives       = mean(false_positive_samples),
    campaign_doses        = mean(campaign_doses)
  ), keyby = scenario],
  digits = 1
)
```

## Paired differences from the baseline

Replicate *i* of every scenario starts from the same school and the same
random draws, so differences within a replicate are effects of the
scenario's settings. "Averted" is baseline minus scenario; positive values
favor the scenario.

```{r}
base <- replicates[scenario == names(scenarios)[1]]
paired <- merge(
  replicates[scenario != names(scenarios)[1]],
  base,
  by       = "replicate",
  suffixes = c("", "_base")
)
knitr::kable(
  paired[, .(
    infections_averted         = mean(infections_base - infections),
    infections_averted_median  = as.numeric(
      median(infections_base - infections)
    ),
    fewer_infections_pct       = 100 * mean(infections < infections_base),
    more_infections_pct        = 100 * mean(infections > infections_base),
    admissions_averted         = mean(admissions_base - admissions),
    hospital_days_averted      = mean(hospital_days_base - hospital_days),
    excluded_days_averted      = mean(
      excluded_student_days_base - excluded_student_days
    ),
    alert_days_added           = mean(alert_days - alert_days_base),
    doses_added                = mean(campaign_doses - campaign_doses_base)
  ), keyby = scenario],
  digits = 1
)
```

## Timeliness

For replicates with at least one reported case, the lead time is the day of
the first case report minus the day the first true-positive wastewater result
arrived (positive values mean wastewater was first). False positives are
excluded.

```{r}
#| include: false
replicates[, lead := first_report_day - first_true_positive_day]
```

```{r}
lead <- replicates[!is.na(first_report_day), .(
  replicates          = .N,
  ww_positive_pct     = 100 * mean(!is.na(first_true_positive_day)),
  ww_first_pct        = 100 * mean(!is.na(lead) & lead > 0),
  lead_days_median    = as.numeric(median(lead, na.rm = TRUE)),
  lead_days_q25       = quantile(lead, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
  lead_days_q75       = quantile(lead, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
), keyby = scenario]
knitr::kable(lead, digits = 1)
```

## Alert timing

Every scenario raises case detection and runs a vaccination campaign during
a public health alert; the
wastewater scenarios can start it before the first case report. Days gained
compares, within each replicate, the day the alert first started in the
baseline (first case report) and in the scenario. Replicates in which the
scenario's first alert followed a false positive before the outbreak was
detected also count as alerts started by wastewater.

```{r}
alerts <- paired[!is.na(first_alert_day_base), .(
  replicates        = .N,
  started_by_ww_pct = 100 * mean(first_alert_trigger == "wastewater"),
  earlier_pct       = 100 * mean(first_alert_day < first_alert_day_base),
  days_gained_q50   = as.numeric(
    median(first_alert_day_base - first_alert_day)
  ),
  days_gained_q75   = quantile(first_alert_day_base - first_alert_day, 0.75),
  days_gained_q90   = quantile(first_alert_day_base - first_alert_day, 0.9)
), keyby = scenario]
knitr::kable(alerts, digits = 1)
```
